title: Helping our Charities Make a Global Impact
what_it_is: Helping our Charities Make a Global Impact

sections.label: Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh
sections.summary: In Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, 656,000 Rohingyas, including 355,300 children, sought sanctuary in the months before the speaker's 2018 visit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the Cox's Bazar region of Bangladesh, 656,000 Rohingyas, including 355,300 children, sought sanctuary in the past few months before my visit back in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: During my visit, I also met some of the 36,373 children who lost at least one parent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A staggering 7,771 innocent little ones lost both mommy and daddy.

sections.label: Matilda and Advocates for Refugees
sections.summary: Matilda set up Advocates for Refugees in 2015 and gathered a strong group of individuals wanting to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is an uphill battle, but Matilda has never given up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: She set up Advocates for Refugees (AFR) in 2015 and has gathered a strong group of individuals, all wanting to do more.

sections.label: Amend Charities Registration Regulations
sections.summary: The first recommendation is to amend the Charities (Registration of Charities) Regulations to allow registration of charities not beneficial wholly or substantially to Singapore's community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first recommendation for this Motion is that we amend our Charities (Registration of Charities) Regulations to allow the registration of charities whose purpose is not beneficial wholly or substantially to the community in Singapore.

sections.label: Fund-Raising Permit Application Delay
sections.summary: They faced problems getting permits; the Fund-Raising for Foreign Charitable Purposes application was submitted in mid-August 2020 and still being processed after 2.5 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, they ran into problems in getting the necessary permits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He submitted the application for a Fund-Raising for Foreign Charitable Purposes (FRFCP) permit in mid-August 2020 and after 2.5 months, the application was still being processed.

sections.label: Streamline permits and waive 80:20
sections.summary: The second recommendation is to streamline and ease the Fund-Raising for Foreign Charitable Purposes permit process; the third is to waive the 80:20 rule for all humanitarian causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second recommendation is that we streamline the process of applying for a Fund-Raising for Foreign Charitable Purposes permit and make it much easier to get.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My third and final recommendation is that we waive the 80:20 rule for all humanitarian causes and not just on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme
sections.summary: Budget 2024 announced 100% tax deduction for donations to overseas humanitarian relief through designated charities under the Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme, a four-year pilot from 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Again, I thank him for listening to their concerns first-hand and seeing how we can help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also thankful that in Budget 2024, we announced that Singaporeans will be able to claim 100% tax deduction for donations to overseas humanitarian relief efforts, under a new scheme launched in recognition of people's desire to do good beyond Singapore's shores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme (OHAS) will run for four years as a pilot, from 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To be eligible for tax deductions under OHAS, donations must be made through designated charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Charities must also have emergency humanitarian assistance as part of their objectives to qualify.

sections.label: Charity registration community benefit condition
sections.summary: One condition for charity registration is that an organisation's purposes must benefit the Singapore community wholly or substantially.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As Mr Ng rightly pointed out, one of the conditions for charity registration is that the purposes of the organisation must be beneficial wholly or substantially to the community in Singapore.

sections.label: Minister's discretion to waive condition
sections.summary: The Minister already has discretion under existing regulations to waive this condition case-by-case and has done so before.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In line with Mr Ng's recommendation, the Minister today already has the discretion under the existing regulations to waive this condition on a case-by-case basis and has done so in the past.

sections.label: Processing applications within 30 days
sections.summary: Over the past three years, most applications were processed within 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In the past three years, we have been able to process most applications within 30 days.

sections.label: Waivers for overseas fund appeals
sections.summary: The COC can waive the rule case-by-case, such as for immediate disaster relief appeals and private donations for foreign charitable causes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This is but one example of appeals that we receive to manage the outflow of funds raised in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: However, the COC can and does, on a case-by-case basis, waive this rule, such as for appeals in aid of providing immediate disaster relief and for private donations raised for foreign charitable causes.

sections.label: OHAS overseas humanitarian assistance pilot
sections.summary: The OHAS is a four-year pilot launched in January, scoped to overseas emergency humanitarian assistance and administered through three designated charities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The OHAS is a four-year pilot recently launched only in January this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The pilot was purposefully scoped to overseas emergency humanitarian assistance to strike a balance between encouraging overseas giving while ensuring that our local charity sector continues to receive the necessary support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This scheme is also administered through designated charities, which are: Mercy Relief Limited, Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation and the Singapore Red Cross Society, to ensure that the necessary governance and controls are in place so that donated funds go to verifiable and legitimate causes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Dialogue and feedback inform policy formulation and reviews, and we are committed to ensure that our legislation and processes remain relevant to the changing landscape of the charity sector in Singapore and the needs of our society.

sections.label: Grantmaker Scheme and public canvassing
sections.summary: Many qualify as grantmakers under the Grantmaker Scheme, but those canvassing publicly for a specific cause do not qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Many actually are qualifying as grantmakers, and they have applied for and have been successfully approved for charity status under the Grantmaker Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, in that sense, if you are going out to the public for appeals, you are going out to canvass on social media in the open for funds coming into a specific cause, then you do not qualify to be a part of this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But I think, the short answer to Mr Louis Ng's question is that, yes, if you are canvassing for refugees overseas, you are not excluded from this exclusion.

sections.label: Fundraising application process for charities
sections.summary: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarifies that some cases take longer due to first-time applications and background checks, not only higher-risk causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, could I just ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary whether helping refugees is considered as one of those higher-risk causes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think to clarify what I have just said, Mr Speaker, I think that what I have mentioned in my speech earlier was that specific instances, especially in the case that the Member has mentioned in his speech, that of Yuan Siang and the Monolith's application, it was the first time that the team has actually put in an application and the Charities Unit team had to go through back and forth, with some hand-holding guidance, especially with regard to checks, background checks, that had to be made to maintain public trust and confidence in the entire fundraising process, to make sure that donors' interests are protected and to make sure that donors are confident that this is a legitimate cause that they are donating towards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, I think that is the angle for which I was coming from when I said that there were certain cases for which the process might be longer, not necessarily only higher risk cases.
